ai_show_review.summary: Experimental early show shines with The Eleven and Dark Star
ai_show_review.blurb: The set features a smoking The Eleven and an expansive Dark Star alongside tight renditions of Morning Dew and He Was A Friend Of Mine. Jerry's guitar stays compelling despite a restless crowd, while the band pushes into loose, exploratory territory. The soundboard capture is fair with analog hiss and occasional splices but remains listenable.
ai_show_review.review: April 12, 1969 at the Student Union Ballroom in Salt Lake City finds the Dead deep in their experimental phase. After a curfew‑forced early first set, the band stretches out on an incendiary The Eleven that showcases Pigpen's organ swirls and Mickey and Billy’s driving dual rhythms. Dark Star erupts later, with Jerry carving soaring leads even as he wrestles with an uneasy audience, and Phil holds down a solid bass foundation throughout. Highlights from the six‑song first set include a heartfelt Morning Dew and a resonant He Was A Friend Of Mine, both delivered with the kind of tight interplay that kept the show moving despite occasional jokes and a few missing moments in the recording.

best_recording.reason: Analog soundboard capture preserves the experimental jams and high energy despite hiss, cuts, and a few splices; it remains the most complete source of this early performance.
